title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 17 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Chronicles chapter 17 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 17 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Chronicles Chapter 17.

questions.question: Where did David say he dwelt when he spoke to Nathan the prophet?
options: In a house of cedars
In a tent
In a palace of gold
In a cave
questions.correctAnswer: In a house of cedars
questions.explanation: David said he dwelt in a house of cedars as stated in 1 Chronicles 17:1.

questions.question: What did Nathan initially tell David to do regarding his heart's desire?
options: Do all that is in thine heart
Wait until God speaks
Build the house immediately
Ask the priests first
questions.correctAnswer: Do all that is in thine heart
questions.explanation: Nathan told David to do all that is in his heart because God is with him, as seen in 1 Chronicles 17:2.

questions.question: When did the word of God come to Nathan about David's desire to build a house?
options: The same night
The next day
After a week
Immediately upon meeting David
questions.correctAnswer: The same night
questions.explanation: The word of God came to Nathan the same night, according to 1 Chronicles 17:3.

questions.question: What command did the LORD give Nathan to tell David?
options: Thou shalt not build me an house to dwell in
Build me an house of cedar
Offer sacrifices on the altar
Gather the people for a feast
questions.correctAnswer: Thou shalt not build me an house to dwell in
questions.explanation: God instructed Nathan to tell David he shall not build Him a house to dwell in, as stated in 1 Chronicles 17:4.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Chronicles 17, God has dwelt in a house since the day He brought up Israel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: God said He has not dwelt in a house since He brought up Israel but moved from tent to tent, as in 1 Chronicles 17:5.

questions.question: According to the LORD, where has He dwelt among Israel before?
options: From tent to tent and tabernacle to tabernacle
In a grand temple of gold
In the mountains
In the city of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: From tent to tent and tabernacle to tabernacle
questions.explanation: God declared He moved from tent to tent and tabernacle to tabernacle since bringing up Israel, as in 1 Chronicles 17:5.

questions.question: Who did the LORD say He commanded to feed His people Israel?
options: Judges of Israel
Priests of the temple
Kings of Egypt
Prophets of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Judges of Israel
questions.explanation: God said He spoke to the judges of Israel whom He commanded to feed His people, found in 1 Chronicles 17:6.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD asked the judges why they had built Him an house of cedars.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: God asked why they had not built Him a house of cedars, not why they had built one, as in 1 Chronicles 17:6.

questions.question: From where did God say He took David to be ruler over Israel?
options: From the sheepcote, even from following the sheep
From the palace of Saul
From the city of Bethlehem
From the battlefield
questions.correctAnswer: From the sheepcote, even from following the sheep
questions.explanation: God said He took David from the sheepcote, even from following the sheep, as stated in 1 Chronicles 17:7.

questions.question: What has God done for David's enemies according to 1 Chronicles 17?
options: Cut off all his enemies from before him
Made peace with his enemies
Exiled his enemies to other lands
Forgiven his enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Cut off all his enemies from before him
questions.explanation: God declared He cut off all David's enemies from before him, as mentioned in 1 Chronicles 17:8.

questions.question: True or False: God promised to ordain a stable place for His people Israel where they would not be moved any more.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: God promised to ordain a place for Israel where they shall dwell and not be moved, as in 1 Chronicles 17:9.

questions.question: According to the LORD, what will He do for David besides subduing his enemies?
options: Build him an house
Make him king of Egypt
Give him many wives
Write a book about him
questions.correctAnswer: Build him an house
questions.explanation: God said He will build David an house besides subduing his enemies, as in 1 Chronicles 17:10.

questions.question: What does God say about David's seed after his days expire?
options: God will raise up his seed and establish his kingdom
His seed will be forgotten
His seed will be cursed
His seed will wander in exile
questions.correctAnswer: God will raise up his seed and establish his kingdom
questions.explanation: God promised to raise up David's seed and establish his kingdom after David's days expire, as stated in 1 Chronicles 17:11.

questions.question: In 1 Chronicles 17, which event comes first?
options: David tells Nathan about the house of cedars
God commands Nathan to tell David he shall not build the house
Nathan tells David to do all that is in his heart
David prays before the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: David tells Nathan about the house of cedars
questions.explanation: David first spoke to Nathan about dwelling in a house of cedars in 1 Chronicles 17:1 before Nathan's response and God's command.

questions.question: True or False: Nathan spoke to David according to all the words and visions the LORD gave him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Nathan delivered to David all words and visions given by the LORD as recorded in 1 Chronicles 17:15.

medium.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 17 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Chronicles Chapter 17 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 17:10, what will the LORD do for David in addition to subduing his enemies?
options: The LORD will build David an house
The LORD will give David many children
The LORD will make David a prophet
The LORD will anoint David as king of all nations
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will build David an house
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 17:10 states that the LORD will subdue all David's enemies and also build him an house, indicating God's promise to establish David's dynasty.

questions.question: What promise does God make about David's descendants in 1 Chronicles 17:11?
options: God will raise up a son from David's seed and establish his kingdom
God will grant David many wives
God will make David's army invincible
God will give David eternal life
questions.correctAnswer: God will raise up a son from David's seed and establish his kingdom
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 17:11 promises that after David's days expire, God will raise up one of his sons and establish his kingdom, showing the continuation of David's royal line.

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 17:12 describe the role of David’s son regarding the house of God?
options: He shall build God an house and God will stablish his throne forever
He will be a priest in the tabernacle
He will lead Israel into battle
He will write the laws of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: He shall build God an house and God will stablish his throne forever
questions.explanation: Verse 12 explains that David’s son will build an house for God and that God will establish his throne forever, emphasizing the eternal covenant with David's lineage.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 17:13, what type of relationship will God have with David’s son?
options: God will be his father, and he shall be God's son
He will be a servant of God
He will be a judge over Israel
He will be a prophet
questions.correctAnswer: God will be his father, and he shall be God's son
questions.explanation: Verse 13 highlights a unique father-son relationship between God and David’s son, signifying a special divine favor and mercy.

questions.question: What does God promise about mercy in 1 Chronicles 17:13 concerning David's descendants?
options: God will not take mercy away from David’s son as He did from the previous king
God will grant mercy only if the son obeys
God will withhold mercy to test the son's faith
God will take mercy away like He did from Saul
questions.correctAnswer: God will not take mercy away from David’s son as He did from the previous king
questions.explanation: The verse assures that the mercy God showed to David’s son will not be taken away as it was from the previous king, referring to Saul, ensuring an enduring covenant.

questions.question: 1 Chronicles 17:14 states that David's son will be settled in God's house and kingdom forever. What does this teach us about God's promises?
options: God’s promises are eternal and unchanging
God’s promises depend on human effort
God’s promises only last for a generation
God’s promises are conditional on sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: God’s promises are eternal and unchanging
questions.explanation: The verse shows that God promises an everlasting kingdom and house for David’s son, teaching that God's covenant is eternal and reliable.

questions.question: How does Nathan communicate God's message to David according to 1 Chronicles 17:15?
options: He speaks all the words and vision exactly as given
He modifies the message to encourage David
He delays delivering the message
He questions God before speaking to David
questions.correctAnswer: He speaks all the words and vision exactly as given
questions.explanation: Verse 15 clarifies that Nathan delivered God’s message to David exactly as it was revealed, showing obedience and faithfulness to God's word.

questions.question: In 1 Chronicles 17:16, David expresses humility before God. What two things does he question about himself?
options: Who he is and what his house is
His wealth and his army's strength
His wisdom and his power
His lineage and his kingdom's size
questions.correctAnswer: Who he is and what his house is
questions.explanation: David humbly questions his own significance and the importance of his house before God, acknowledging God's greatness (verse 16).

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 17:17, why does David consider God's promise to be a great honor?
options: Because God has spoken of David's house for a long time and regarded him highly
Because David has built many houses for the LORD
Because David has defeated many enemies
Because David is the wealthiest king
questions.correctAnswer: Because God has spoken of David's house for a long time and regarded him highly
questions.explanation: David acknowledges that God has honored him greatly by promising a lasting dynasty and regarding him as a man of high degree (verse 17).

questions.question: What does David express in 1 Chronicles 17:18 regarding his ability to honor God more in prayer?
options: He feels he cannot speak more because God knows him
He plans to offer many sacrifices
He wants to build a bigger temple
He decides to write songs of praise
questions.correctAnswer: He feels he cannot speak more because God knows him
questions.explanation: David says he cannot speak more for the honor of God’s servant because God already knows him well, expressing humility and reverence (verse 18).

questions.question: What lesson about faith and trust can be drawn from 1 Chronicles 17:19 where David acknowledges God's greatness for doing all these things?
options: God fulfills His promises according to His own heart and faithfulness
Human effort alone guarantees God's blessings
Only David's wisdom brings success
God changes His mind frequently
questions.correctAnswer: God fulfills His promises according to His own heart and faithfulness
questions.explanation: David recognizes that God's greatness is demonstrated by fulfilling promises according to His heart, teaching believers to trust God's faithful character (verse 19).

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 17:20 say about the uniqueness of the LORD?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 20 affirms that there is none like the LORD and no God besides Him, emphasizing the unique and incomparable nature of God.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 17:21, what has God done for Israel that sets them apart from other nations?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse states God redeemed Israel to be His own people and made a great name by driving out other nations, showing Israel's distinct status (verse 21).

questions.question: Does 1 Chronicles 17:22 say that Israel is God's people forever?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 22 clearly states that God made Israel His own people forever, and He became their God, confirming the eternal covenant.

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 17:23 ask God to do concerning His promise to David and his house?
options: Establish the promise forever and do as He said
Delay the promise until Israel is ready
Allow David to build the temple first
Test David's faith with hardships
questions.correctAnswer: Establish the promise forever and do as He said
questions.explanation: David prays that God would firmly establish His promise to him and his house forever and fulfill what He has spoken (verse 23).

hard.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 17 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Chronicles Chapter 17.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 17:19, why has the LORD done all this greatness and made known these great things?
options: For David's enemies
For the sake of the servant and according to God's own heart
For the people of Israel only
For the temple building
questions.correctAnswer: For the sake of the servant and according to God's own heart
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 17:19 states that the LORD has done all this greatness for the servant's sake and according to His own heart, indicating a personal divine purpose in His actions.

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 17:20 affirm about the LORD in comparison to other gods?
options: There are many gods like Him
He is one among many gods
There is none like Him, nor any God beside Him
He is a god among the gods
questions.correctAnswer: There is none like Him, nor any God beside Him
questions.explanation: Verse 20 clearly affirms the uniqueness of the LORD, stating there is none like Him and no God beside Him, emphasizing monotheism.

questions.question: Which nation is described as unique and chosen by God in 1 Chronicles 17:21?
options: Egypt
Babylon
Israel
Assyria
questions.correctAnswer: Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 21 praises Israel as the unique nation redeemed by God to be His own people, highlighting their special covenant relationship.

questions.question: In 1 Chronicles 17:22, what relationship does God establish with Israel?
options: God made Israel a temporary ally
God rejected Israel
God made Israel His own people forever and became their God
God made Israel a servant nation
questions.correctAnswer: God made Israel His own people forever and became their God
questions.explanation: Verse 22 states that God made Israel His own people forever and became their God, confirming the everlasting covenant.

questions.question: What does David ask God to do concerning the promise about his house in 1 Chronicles 17:23?
options: Forget the promise
Change the promise
Establish the thing spoken concerning his servant and his house forever
Delay the promise
questions.correctAnswer: Establish the thing spoken concerning his servant and his house forever
questions.explanation: David prays for the establishment of God's promise concerning his house forever, as stated in verse 23.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 17:24, what is the intended effect of establishing David's house before God?
options: To diminish God's name
To magnify God's name forever
To honor other gods
To separate David's house from God
questions.correctAnswer: To magnify God's name forever
questions.explanation: Verse 24 emphasizes that establishing David's house serves to magnify the LORD's name forever, showing God's glory through His covenant.

questions.question: Why has David found it in his heart to pray before God according to 1 Chronicles 17:25?
options: Because God told him He would build David a house
Because he wanted to build the temple himself
Because he was afraid of his enemies
Because he wanted wealth
questions.correctAnswer: Because God told him He would build David a house
questions.explanation: David's motivation to pray comes from God's promise to build him an house, as expressed in verse 25.

questions.question: In 1 Chronicles 17:26, how does David describe God's promise to him?
options: As uncertain and vague
As a promise of punishment
As promised goodness
As a request from David
questions.correctAnswer: As promised goodness
questions.explanation: David acknowledges God's promise as one of goodness, affirming God's gracious intent in verse 26.

questions.question: What does David ask God to do for his house in 1 Chronicles 17:27?
options: Destroy it
Bless it so it may be before God forever
Forget it
Ignore it
questions.correctAnswer: Bless it so it may be before God forever
questions.explanation: David prays for God's blessing upon his house so it may endure before God forever, as stated in verse 27.

questions.question: Which of the following Bible passages is most directly connected to the promise that God will build David an eternal house as stated in 1 Chronicles 17:11-14?
options: Psalm 89:3-4
Exodus 20:1-17
Genesis 1:1-2
Revelation 21:1-4
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 89:3-4
questions.explanation: Psalm 89:3-4 echoes God's covenant promise to David about establishing his house forever, directly connecting to 1 Chronicles 17:11-14.

questions.question: The literary device primarily used in 1 Chronicles 17:7-14, where God's promises to David are structured with repeating parallel thoughts, is known as what?
options: Chiasm
Allegory
Metaphor
Parable
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: The section from verses 7 to 14 uses chiasm, a literary device involving mirrored parallelism, to emphasize God's promises to David.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated as "house" in the promise to David in 1 Chronicles 17:11, and how does it relate to the concept of David's dynasty?
options: "Bayit" meaning a physical building only
"Bayit" meaning family lineage or dynasty
"Elohim" meaning God
"Torah" meaning law
questions.correctAnswer: "Bayit" meaning family lineage or dynasty
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word "bayit" used for "house" in verse 11 often denotes not just a physical structure but also a family lineage or dynasty, relating to God's promise of an enduring dynasty for David.

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 17:21-22 reflect the theme of God's redemption and covenant faithfulness seen earlier in Exodus?
options: By focusing on temple rituals only
By recalling God's redemption of Israel from Egypt and establishing them as His people forever
By describing the building of altars
By ignoring Israel's history
questions.correctAnswer: By recalling God's redemption of Israel from Egypt and establishing them as His people forever
questions.explanation: Verses 21-22 reflect the theme from Exodus where God redeemed Israel from Egypt and made them His covenant people forever, emphasizing continuity of divine faithfulness.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Chronicles 17:20, the LORD is described as one among many gods.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 20 clearly states there is none like the LORD and no God beside Him, affirming His uniqueness and denying polytheism.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Chronicles 17:19 indicates that God's actions were motivated by His own heart as well as for the servant's sake.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 19 emphasizes that God acted both for the servant's sake and according to His own heart, indicating divine intentionality.

theological.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 17 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Chronicles Chapter 17 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What reason does God give Nathan for not allowing David to build Him a house to dwell in?
options: God has never dwelt in a house but moved from tent to tent
David’s heart was not right before God
God preferred Solomon to build the house
The ark was not yet ready to be housed
questions.correctAnswer: God has never dwelt in a house but moved from tent to tent
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 17:5 states that God has not dwelt in a house since He brought up Israel but has moved from tent to tent, explaining why David was not to build Him a house.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated by God’s promise to raise up David’s seed and establish his kingdom forever?
options: Omnipresence
Eternal faithfulness
Justice
Wrath
questions.correctAnswer: Eternal faithfulness
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 17:11-14 show God's eternal faithfulness in promising to establish David’s throne forever and not removing His mercy from his descendants.

questions.question: How does David respond to God’s promises concerning his house and kingdom?
options: With humility and praise acknowledging his smallness
With anger and disbelief
By immediately building a temple
By seeking a sign from God
questions.correctAnswer: With humility and praise acknowledging his smallness
questions.explanation: In 1 Chronicles 17:16-17, David humbly questions his own worth and the significance of his house, showing reverence and praise to God for His promises.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by God’s declaration, 'I will be his father, and he shall be my son'?
options: The doctrine of the Davidic Covenant
The doctrine of the Trinity
The doctrine of original sin
The doctrine of justification by faith
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of the Davidic Covenant
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 17:13 reveals the covenantal relationship between God and David’s descendants, foundational for the Davidic Covenant doctrine.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 17:9, what has God promised concerning the security of Israel?
options: Israel will be planted and dwell in their place without being moved or wasted by wickedness
Israel will conquer all surrounding nations permanently
Israel will live in exile until the Messiah comes
Israel must build many houses for God
questions.correctAnswer: Israel will be planted and dwell in their place without being moved or wasted by wickedness
questions.explanation: Verse 9 promises that God will ordain a place for Israel where they will dwell securely and not be harmed by wickedness as before.

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 17:8 reveal about God’s active role in David’s life?
options: God has been with David wherever he went and cut off David’s enemies
God only occasionally assisted David
David succeeded by his own strength
David’s enemies remained undefeated
questions.correctAnswer: God has been with David wherever he went and cut off David’s enemies
questions.explanation: Verse 8 emphasizes God’s omnipresence and sovereign power in supporting David by removing his enemies and establishing his fame.

questions.question: Which combined teaching do verses 5-6 and verse 11 convey about God's presence and promise?
options: God has not dwelt in houses but promises to raise a lasting dynasty through David’s seed
God will dwell in a house built by David immediately
God rejects David’s family permanently
God’s presence is limited to the tabernacle only
questions.correctAnswer: God has not dwelt in houses but promises to raise a lasting dynasty through David’s seed
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 explain God’s historical presence in tents, while verse 11 promises a future lasting dynasty through David’s descendants, combining God’s transcendence with covenantal faithfulness.

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 17:10 teach about God's sovereignty over Israel's enemies?
options: God will subdue all David’s enemies and establish judges over Israel
Israel must fight alone without divine help
David’s enemies will rule Israel
Judges will be ineffective
questions.correctAnswer: God will subdue all David’s enemies and establish judges over Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 10 reveals God’s sovereign authority to defeat enemies and ordain leaders over Israel, highlighting divine governance.

questions.question: How does the chapter 17 portrayal of God’s relationship with Israel contrast with pagan gods, according to David’s prayer in verses 20-21?
options: God is unique and has redeemed Israel to be His own people, unlike other nations’ gods
God is one among many gods
Israel’s gods are more powerful
God is distant and uninvolved
questions.correctAnswer: God is unique and has redeemed Israel to be His own people, unlike other nations’ gods
questions.explanation: Verses 20-21 affirm the uniqueness of God, who alone redeems and claims Israel as His people, contrasting pagan deities who do not redeem.

questions.question: What synthesis can be drawn from verses 24 and 27 about God's purpose in establishing David’s house?
options: To magnify God’s name and ensure David’s house is blessed forever
To make David’s house wealthy and powerful
To separate David’s family from Israel permanently
To abolish Israel’s monarchy
questions.correctAnswer: To magnify God’s name and ensure David’s house is blessed forever
questions.explanation: Verses 24 and 27 together show that God’s establishment of David’s house serves to magnify His name and secure perpetual blessing.

questions.question: What apologetic response does 1 Chronicles 17 provide against the sceptic’s claim that God’s promises to David were merely political and temporary?
options: God’s covenant promises include an eternal kingdom and father-son relationship, transcending political conditions
God’s promises were later revoked
David’s kingdom quickly fell and was insignificant
God made no real promises to David
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant promises include an eternal kingdom and father-son relationship, transcending political conditions
questions.explanation: Verses 11-14 affirm an everlasting covenant establishing David’s throne forever, refuting claims that the promises were temporary or merely political.

questions.question: What does Nathan initially tell David in response to his desire to build a house for God in verse 2?
options: Do all that is in thine heart; for God is with thee
Stop and do not build anything
Wait for God’s direct command
Build the temple immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Do all that is in thine heart; for God is with thee
questions.explanation: Verse 2 records Nathan encouraging David to proceed because God was with him, though God later corrects Nathan’s initial message.

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 17:7-8 emphasize God’s initiative and grace in David’s rise to kingship?
options: God took David from being a shepherd and was with him, cutting off enemies and making him famous
David earned kingship by his own efforts
David was chosen because of his military might alone
God was distant during David’s rise
questions.correctAnswer: God took David from being a shepherd and was with him, cutting off enemies and making him famous
questions.explanation: Verses 7-8 highlight God’s sovereign call and sustaining presence in David’s life, demonstrating divine grace in his leadership.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's mercy is taught in 1 Chronicles 17:13?
options: God will not take away His mercy from David’s descendants as He did from Saul
God’s mercy is conditional and often withdrawn
God’s mercy is extended only to Israel’s judges
God’s mercy depends on temple sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: God will not take away His mercy from David’s descendants as He did from Saul
questions.explanation: Verse 13 teaches the doctrine of God’s covenantal mercy, showing He maintains His favor with David’s line unlike the previous king Saul.

questions.question: How does David describe God’s treatment of him in 1 Chronicles 17:19 in relation to God’s own heart?
options: God has done greatness according to His own heart for David’s sake
God has been indifferent to David
David’s greatness is due to his own merit
God has punished David severely
questions.correctAnswer: God has done greatness according to His own heart for David’s sake
questions.explanation: Verse 19 shows David acknowledging that God’s mighty acts for him are aligned with God’s own loving and gracious heart.
